name: Aurelius Collective Voile Dress Shirt — Port-Open
description: A crisp white voile dress shirt with a Mandarin-adjacent collar and mother-of-pearl resin buttons, cut to skim rather than drape. Pre-cut neural port openings at the standard C3 and C5 positions are finished with brushed titanium grommets so they read as intentional design elements rather than medical accommodations. Packaged unstarched; it holds a press for exactly one day.
functionality: Neural port access grommets at C3/C5, breathable voile weave for summer humidity, semi-spread collar.
what_it_says: Your augmentation is not something you hide — it's something you frame.
story_hooks: A batch shipped with grommet placements 4mm off-standard — wearers with precise port positions have been complaining loudly on the Aurelius community boards.
The voile is thin enough that a subdermal implant network is faintly visible through the fabric in certain lighting — some wearers consider this a feature.

physical_description.visual_profile: A pristine white voile shirt with an architectural quality—structured yet ethereal. The Mandarin-adjacent collar sits high and precise. Two brushed titanium grommets at the nape and mid-back read as avant-garde design accents rather than functional ports, giving the wearer an air of deliberate augmentation chic. The fabric catches light like water, creating subtle play across the chest and shoulders.
physical_description.fit: Skim-cut, neither fitted nor loose—follows the body's contours without compression. Designed to move with rather than cling to the wearer, allowing visibility of port grommets and any subcutaneous tech beneath.
physical_description.primary_material: Voile—a lightweight, high-thread-count synthetic blend with a slight sheen. Treated for wrinkle resistance but intentionally engineered to hold a crisp press for exactly 24 hours, forcing intentional maintenance.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost gossamer to the touch, with a subtle weave pattern visible under direct light. The brushed titanium grommets have a matte, tactile finish that contrasts with the fluid fabric.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pure white with warm ivory undertones. Mother-of-pearl resin buttons catch ambient light in iridescent flashes—soft pinks, greens, and silvers depending on angle.
physical_description.closures: Mother-of-pearl resin buttons running center-front, paired with precision button holes. No visible snaps or magnetic alternatives—pure analog closure as a subtle luxury signal.
distinctive_features: Pre-cut neural port openings at C3 and C5 spine positions
Brushed titanium grommets finishing port openings—designed to read as intentional aesthetic rather than medical necessity
Mother-of-pearl resin buttons with warm iridescent quality
24-hour press retention engineering—built-in obsolescence disguised as haute couture
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury. The price point, materials, and intentional design accommodation signal corpo elite or high-tier independent augmentation enthusiasts.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by augmented individuals who want to signal integration of chrome and flesh as aesthetic choice rather than necessity. Corporate boardrooms, upscale neural clinics, indie biotech circles. The wearer is comfortable with visible augmentation but frames it as design statement rather than disability or survival hack.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine for the first 24 hours post-wear, then requires re-pressing or acceptance of soft wrinkles. Usually seen freshly laundered and pressed, creating an aspirational quality—this shirt demands daily ritual.
